approach: Write the constant-length constraint between the horizontal position of A and the vertical position of B, then differentiate with respect to time.

steps.text: Let x be the horizontal distance of A from the corner and y be the height of B on the wall. The rod length is fixed.
steps.equation: x² + y² = l², with x = l cos θ, y = l sin θ

steps.text: Differentiate the constraint with respect to time.
End A moves away from the wall at the given constant speed v, so dx/dt = v. Substitute x = l cos θ and y = l sin θ.

steps.equation: dy/dt = −v cos θ / sin θ = −v cot θ
steps.why_this_step: The negative sign shows y is decreasing, meaning B moves downward at this rate.

final_answer.value: The velocity of end B is v cot θ, directed downward.

common_mistakes.text: Differentiating x = l cos θ and y = l sin θ but mismatching which trigonometric ratio goes with dx/dt gives v tan θ instead of the correct v cot θ.
